target_customer: Software vendors (ISVs) that must deploy and update their product in customers' on-prem, VPC, BYOC and air-gapped environments
problem: Vendors shipping self-hosted software struggle to deploy, update and support it inside customer environments.
business_model: Open source core (Distr) with a commercial software distribution platform
product_category: Developer tools, software distribution for self-hosted software

founders.name: Philip Miglinci
previous_startups: A startup with co-founder, per the company description
founders.background_notes: The company description says he was CTO of a European Kubernetes-based company acquired in 2022; the YC page describes the CTO role as at alerting infrastructure.

founders.name: Louis Weston
prior_employers: A fintech startup of over 100 employees (intern to legal counsel)
founders.background_notes: Business, law and compliance background per the YC page.

competitors.name: Helm
competitors.what: The standard Kubernetes package manager that Glasskube positioned against

competitors.name: Kustomize
competitors.what: Template free Kubernetes configuration customization, compared on speed and dependency handling

technical_complexity.rationale: A Kubernetes package manager with operators, dependency handling and a UI is standard cloud native engineering, and the later software distribution platform adds controllers and air-gapped support. The CTO was experienced with Kubernetes.

defensibility.rationale: Open source under Apache 2.0 means anyone can copy it, and Helm has a dominant installed base. Customer deployments managed through the control plane create some lock in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Helm remained the default. No acquisition or copying event was found.

market_need_then: Kubernetes users reported pain points with Helm, per the founders' launch posts. Later the company reported 200 plus organizations and 1,200 plus GitHub stars for Distr, its own claims.

branding.domain_note: Product site is distr.sh while the company stays Glasskube, Inc.

identity.logo: Glasskube logo on GitHub with an ice cube emoji tagline
identity.voice_and_tone: Open source, building in public, launch weeks and Show HN posts

branding.brand_signature: Open source launches on Show HN and Discord community
branding.community_and_virality: A Discord community of contributors, a 1k stars milestone post and a CNCF landscape listing, per DEV Community posts seen in search results.

brand_strength.rationale: Developer community traction under the Glasskube name for the package manager, but the new product carries the Distr brand and the Glasskube name no longer describes it.

pivots.from: Open source Kubernetes package manager (Glasskube, alpha Feb 2024)
pivots.to: Distr, an open source software distribution platform for self-hosted deployments
pivots.why: Not stated in sources opened; the YC page shows the shift in positioning.

outcome_analysis: Glasskube launched an open source Kubernetes package manager in early 2024, joined YC Summer 2024, then repositioned to Distr, a software distribution platform for vendors shipping on-prem. Open source traction is claimed with 200 plus organizations and 1,200 plus stars, but no verified funding was found and the open source license limits defensibility. The pivot suggests the package manager alone did not find a paying market.
notes: Aggregators disagree: VCBacked lists 500K pre-seed in Aug 2024, CB Insights lists a Seed VC round on 2024-09-20 with Y Combinator, Pioneer Fund and Eight Capital Group, Dealroom lists 125K. No primary source, so nothing recorded as a round. Founded year 2023 per YC page. Education only partly stated. Pivot date not sourced. Competitor traction and funding not stated in the InfoQ coverage seen in search results.
